findings.claim: The stale-wording test pins 'repository bound to a workflow' and similar phrases as absent from every OpenCode text, which is a brittle substring check. A harmless future rewording that reuses one of these phrases (for example 'a repository bound to a workflow' in an unrelated claim) fails the test even when the claim is accurate. The test also does not cover the Claude skills claim, which is pinned separately.

The memory-enforcement claim names a subtest ('OpencodeAdaptsBeforeGate') by a bare string. The test only checks that the claim text contains this name. Nothing verifies the subtest exists in cmd:TestCodexSourceProcesses, so renaming it leaves the claim citing a nonexistent proof while the declaration test still passes.

evidence: Both changed paths were read in the diff. Every wording change in declarations.go has a matching pin in the declaration test.
The added Claude skills test reference installer:TestUnrelatedSkillUnchanged is pinned by TestClaudeSkillsClaimKeepsTheUnrelatedSkillTest.
No behavior, runtime or installer code changed, so no regression on previously valid input is visible.
